How to choose between them

Florals are the obvious entry

Lavender, ylang ylang and the absolutes are what most people picture. They are also the most polarising — ylang ylang and tuberose divide opinion sharply, so start small.

Woods last longest in a room

Cedarwood, vetiver, sandalwood and patchouli sit low and slow. They hold a blend together and are still noticeable hours after a floral has gone.

Herbaceous oils suit people who dislike sweetness

Roman chamomile, clary sage and marjoram are soft without being sugary, which makes them easier to live with night after night.

How people use these

◌

Diffuse before bed

Four to six drops an hour before sleep. More does not work better — it flattens the scent.

✋

Dilute for a body oil

Two per cent in jojoba — roughly 12 drops per 30 ml — massaged into wrists or the soles of the feet.

♨

Build a blend

A wood underneath, a floral on top. One drop of an absolute is enough to change the whole thing.

Questions about relaxation oils

Which oil is best for sleep?

We cannot make that claim, and nobody honestly can. What we can say is that lavender is overwhelmingly the one people buy for their evening routine, followed by cedarwood and the Deep Sleep style blends. Scent is good at signalling to you that the day is ending; it is not a sedative.

What is the difference between an essential oil and an absolute?

Extraction. Essential oils are distilled; absolutes are extracted with solvents, because flowers like jasmine, rose and tuberose are destroyed by the heat of distillation. Absolutes carry trace solvent residue by nature of the process, which is worth knowing before you buy one.

Can I diffuse these overnight?

We would not. Run a diffuser for 30 to 60 minutes and let it stop. Olfactory fatigue means you stop registering the smell within minutes anyway, so an all-night session mostly wastes oil.

Which of these are safe in pregnancy?

Several in this collection are commonly advised against — clary sage, marjoram, davana and the absolutes among them. Each product page states its own position, but speak to a doctor rather than relying on a website.
